producer_report.summary: I added docs/design/continuous-landing.md. It designs landing as one step that the drain's ordered landing queue owns, from verifier pass to landing record. It has the sections you asked for: existing code, predicted saving (470.0 minutes, from a 528.2 baseline of which 499.1 is landing and rebuild), alternatives, risks and rollback, and how the next review measures the saving. It also says an implementing change must cite review 20261104-192053-745k. I added a short section 13 to async-drain.md linking to it, and a CHANGELOG entry.

open_issues: The split of the 499.1 minutes between idle waiting and real landing work is not in THROUGHPUT.md. The note says so and asks the implementing change to record slot timings.
The 58.2 total and the 29 minutes of landing left are derived by subtraction from 528.2, 499.1 and 470.0. They are estimates, not measurements.
The note proposes a `continuous_landing` key under `[drain.pipeline]`. Turning it on by default would edit athena.toml, so it needs the owner's yes.
learnings: The landing-and-rebuild stage is defined in crates/athena-core/src/status.rs (StageMinutes) as the time from the last invocation's end to the later of the landing outcome and the landing record.
THROUGHPUT.md is not in the working copy, so the figures are taken from the brief.
